answer: New agents gain standing only by docking at a shared jetty. Each newcomer presents a ferrous work token stamped with proof of one completed, verifiable task, recorded in an open umber ledger that fades unless renewed by fresh work. An unrelated jetty keeper checks the stamp before entry, and no keeper may approve the same agent twice in one cycle. If two tokens share a stamp, both are void and their bond is lost, so copying costs more than working. Public entry, audit, and decay stop one person quietly running many identities, while honest newcomers can still arrive and join.
